long_biography.plain_text:
Born into a musical family in Chiswick, West London, Townshend studied graphic design at Ealing School of Art and absorbed performance art alongside American blues. He joined Roger Daltrey and John Entwistle in the group that became the Who, emerging as its guitarist, principal songwriter and conceptual leader. His early writing turned youthful alienation into concise singles while his physical, windmill guitar style made the band instantly recognisable.

Townshend broadened that framework through the narrative albums Tommy and Quadrophenia, later adapting his work for film, theatre and ballet. He also recorded solo albums, wrote fiction and an autobiography, and worked in book publishing. Songwriting, recordings, touring and adaptations created the core music-rights fortune. He has continued to reshape older work for new formats while pursuing fresh performance and writing projects.
